column1: # Every constructor in crates/rexx-exec/src whose return type is Loud or Raised,
# with the surface its construction sites are on and, for the ones a message send
# itself can produce, whether an instance-receiver probe reached that site and how
# Derived, not written: crates/rexx-exec/tests/refusal_sites.rs re-derives columns
# 1 to 4 from the source on every run and fails if this file disagrees, so a
# constructor added later is red here rather than silently unwalked. That test also
# holds the `answer` column against the constructor's own source, in both
# surface -- which files the construction sites are in. `send` is dispatch.rs
# (outside its #[cfg(test)] mod tests) and dispatch/native.rs, where
# Interp::send_message and Interp::enter_method_body both are; `ir` is ir.rs
# verdict, for the `send` rows only -- about the program in the witness column:
#   agrees    probed against the oracle on both engines, three descriptors and
#   diverges  probed and does not agree. Every one is in the Task 9 report with
#   recorded  a divergence the phase plan records as not to be built.
#   not-run   the shape is in corpus/oracle-crashes.txt and must never be run.
#   off-send-surface  no construction site the send machinery reaches.
# reached -- whether the probe reached THIS constructor rather than a check that
# fires first. `yes` requires `answer` to be an identifier the constructor itself
# can produce: an "M.N" it builds with syntax(M, N), or text at its own definition
# or at one of its construction sites. `no` requires `answer` to be none of those,
# and to say why there is no route. The test enforces both directions, so a row
# cannot be marked reached without its own identifier or unreached while carrying
# witness -- the program, spelled the way it has to be spelled. Where a nearby
# spelling agrees, the row says so: a reader who tries the obvious one, sees
# byte-identical output and deletes the row is the failure this column exists to
# The test does not re-run a probe: the `witness` column is prose rather than a
# runnable program, and re-running one would need it to be a program.
# (Integration-test binaries under crates/rexx-exec/tests/ do reach the oracle
# through support::oracle -- licensed_divergences.rs among them -- so the
# obstacle is this column's medium and not the tooling.) `answer` therefore
# ties the row to the source, not to the transcript.
# Two constructors may share an "M.N", and where they do this check cannot tell
# their rows apart: transposing both the `answer` and the `witness` of
# (88.914), leaves every test in refusal_sites.rs green. Measured, both pairs.
# Those are the only such pairs, and
# that sentence true rather than merely written down.
